chapter: War years, Goodman and Woody Herman
title: A ten-piece band in Boston with Linda Keene
summary: Leaving MCA, he forms a ten-piece band with Conrad Gozzo, Rusty Dedrick and singer Linda Keene, managed by Cy Shribman, whose players went to Thornhill.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: Well, I'd formed another little band --
And I tried to break my contract with MCA --
And I went up to Boston and worked for Cy and formed another band, which I had -- I formed a 10-piece band.
-- which was kind of a -- with Conrad Gazzo Gazzo and Rusty Dedrick Dedrich, and it was kind of a nice band, it was kind of a challenge with three brass and three saxes -- three rhythm.
Linda Keene was singing and just to try and do something with that.
And it turned out it was a very ---
-- wild, singing band. It was -- we'd play opposite big bands in Atlantic City --
-- really -- we had a good rhythm section, it swung, I forgot all the guys, but they were -- they were a happy bunch of guys, they really enjoyed playing.
And I -- it was very good. Then, I got into bigger -- added a few more, later. And --

So this in a sense from a professional point of view, you and Mildred weren't -- you were on separate lines, I mean she was getting separate bookings here and there and there were theaters occasionally, and so on --
Well, she was really taking it easy most of the time.
Well a few, yes. She made --
-- oh, I don't know, she made some with Eldridge well, Teddy and Roy Albers and the woodwinds --
-- she made 'All The Things You Are,' and 'Fools Rush In' and --
-- and she made some more like that. She was making records every once in awhile -- yes.
But you were on the road --
Yeah, I was in and out of the place. I'd go and I'd come back and --
-- and after awhile when I'd -- I'd get most of those guys -- I had Barney Galbreath and a bench in that band and I still wasn't satisfied with it, so I really got away from MCA at that time --
So Cy Scribner talked me to saying -- talk to the guys, maybe they'd go with Claude Thornhill -- I said -- they all -- most of them did.
That's when he was opening out in Glen Gozzo Island area, Gazzo and Rusty and Ted Goddard -- [End of Reel III]
So most of them went with -- most of the fellas in that band went with Claude Thornhill.
